claim: The superficial epithelial layer that initially covers the deep regions of double IMZs retracts to a small area, leaving most of the deep region uncovered, a behavior associated with CT of the IMZ but one that does not occur in the double NIMZs.

evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 3A and Video 9.

claim: Convergence of the IMZ explants is accompanied by thickening, whereas NIMZ explants show no thickening.
source: Lastly, convergence of the IMZ explants is accompanied by thickening, whereas NIMZ explants show no thickening (Figure 3B and D; Video 10*).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 3B, 3D, and Video 10.

claim: Convergence of Double IMZ explants showed an initial rapid phase, which correlated with the rapid thickening of the IMZ observed in the first hour after release of the initial VMZ sandwich explants from the cover glass.
source: Convergence of Double IMZ explants showed an initial rapid phase (Figure 3C, G + 2–3 h), which correlated with the rapid thickening of the IMZ observed in the first hour after release of the initial VMZ sandwich explants from the cover glass (data not shown), during the lateral healing together of the two IMZs (see Figure 1—figure supplement 1A8).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 3C.

claim: A slower convergence phase followed the initial rapid phase, which correlated with the continuing, slower thickening of the Double IMZ explants.
source: A slower convergence phase followed, which correlated with the continuing, slower thickening of the Double IMZ explants (Figure 3C and D, G + 3 h onward).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: Double NIMZ explants showed only slow mediolateral convergence, and did not thicken.
source: In contrast, Double NIMZ explants showed only slow mediolateral convergence, and did not thicken (Figure 3C and D), but it did slowly elongate orthogonally within the horizontal plane, that is along the initially shorter animal-vegetal axis, making the explant more circular (Figure 3A, Video 9).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 3C, 3D, 3A, and Video 9.

claim: Double NIMZ explants slowly elongate orthogonally within the horizontal plane, that is along the initially shorter animal-vegetal axis, making the explant more circular.
source: In contrast, Double NIMZ explants showed only slow mediolateral convergence, and did not thicken (Figure 3C and D), but it did slowly elongate orthogonally within the horizontal plane, that is along the initially shorter animal-vegetal axis, making the explant more circular (Figure 3A, Video 9).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 3A and Video 9.

claim: Neither the Double IMZ nor NIMZ explants showed apparent differences in convergence or thickening in the animal vs. vegetal edges within the tissue.
source: Neither the Double IMZ nor NIMZ explants showed apparent differences in convergence or thickening in the animal vs. vegetal edges within the tissue, illustrating that CT does not show the patterned anterior-to-posterior progression characteristic of CE (Shih and Keller, 1992b; Lane and Keller, 1997).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by citations to Shih and Keller, 1992b; Lane and Keller, 1997.

claim: CT does not show the patterned anterior-to-posterior progression characteristic of CE.
source: Neither the Double IMZ nor NIMZ explants showed apparent differences in convergence or thickening in the animal vs. vegetal edges within the tissue, illustrating that CT does not show the patterned anterior-to-posterior progression characteristic of CE (Shih and Keller, 1992b; Lane and Keller, 1997).
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the results presented and supported by citations to Shih and Keller, 1992b; Lane and Keller, 1997.

claim: In intact embryos, the pre-involution IMZ does not thicken during early gastrulation but instead continues to thin.
source: In intact embryos, the pre-involution IMZ does not thicken during early gastrulation but instead continues to thin (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B), as does the NIMZ (Keller, 1980).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B, and a citation to Keller, 1980.

claim: Thickening of the IMZ is prevented by the mechanical resistance to its convergence by adjacent tissues, notably the vegetal endoderm.
source: Thickening of the IMZ is prevented by the mechanical resistance to its convergence by adjacent tissues, notably the vegetal endoderm (See Discussion).
evidence: The claim is stated as an inference.

claim: Beginning around Stage 10-, the epithelial tissue lying over the lower deep IMZ began to retract and/or self-adhere (basal to basal), reducing its contact area, whereas the epithelium over the deep AC-NIMZ region remained stable or spread further over time.
source: Beginning around Stage 10-, the epithelial tissue lying over the lower deep IMZ began to retract and/or self-adhere (basal to basal; see Luu et al., 2011), reducing its contact area, whereas the epithelium over the deep AC-NIMZ region remained stable or spread further over time (Figure 4B and C; Video 11*).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 4B, 4C, Video 11, and a citation to Luu et al., 2011.

claim: Transplanted epithelium over deep ectoderm does not spread until Stage 10-.
source: Notably, transplanted epithelium over deep ectoderm does not spread until Stage 10- (Figure 4C); the same is true of endogenous epithelium adjacent to naked deep ectoderm (DRS, personal observations).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding and supported by Figure 4C and personal observations.

claim: In experiments where the deep tissue was cultured on a BSA coated substrate with patches of epithelium spanning the IMZ-NIMZ boundary, the epithelium contracted and retreated from the surface of the deep IMZ onto the surface of the deep NIMZ, where it re-spread.
source: Under these conditions, the epithelium contracted and retreated from the surface of the deep IMZ onto the surface of the deep NIMZ, where it re-spread (Figure 4E); note that the deep cells of the IMZ spread upward and over the deep NIMZ cells (Figure 4E), such that they appear to follow or push the epithelium as it retreats animally, a behavior more easily appreciated in the time lapse recording (Video 12*).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 4E and Video 12.

claim: The deep cells of the IMZ spread upward and over the deep NIMZ cells, such that they appear to follow or push the epithelium as it retreats animally.
source: note that the deep cells of the IMZ spread upward and over the deep NIMZ cells (Figure 4E), such that they appear to follow or push the epithelium as it retreats animally, a behavior more easily appreciated in the time lapse recording (Video 12*).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 4E and Video 12.

claim: The affinity between superficial epithelium and IMZ cells decreases at Stage 10- (G-0.7h), while that between epithelium and NIMZ cells increases.
source: These results support the idea that the affinity between superficial epithelium and IMZ cells decreases at Stage 10- (G-0.7h), while that between epithelium and NIMZ cells increases.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the results presented.

claim: It is the deep IMZ tissue that lowers its affinity for the overlying epithelium around the beginning of gastrulation (Stage 10, G0), rather than the epithelium changing its affinity for the deep IMZ.
source: The changes in spreading or contraction behavior occur regardless of the region of the embryo from which the epithelium was taken (e.g. AC/NIMZ vs. IMZ superficial epithelium), which strongly suggests that it is the deep IMZ tissue that lowers its affinity for the overlying epithelium around the beginning of gastrulation (Stage 10, G0), rather than the epithelium changing its affinity for the deep IMZ.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the results presented.

claim: The IFT of IMZ wonton explants increases, nearly doubling by G + 1.5 h, beginning between Stages 9.5 and 10 (G-1h to G0), but no increase is seen in AC sandwich or wonton explants.
source: We saw increasing IFT of IMZ wonton explants beginning between Stages 9.5 and 10 (G-1h to G0), nearly doubling by G + 1.5 h, but no increase in AC sandwich or wonton explants (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 5C.

claim: The TST of mesodermal deep tissue aggregates remained low until after Stage 10, when it increased more than twofold, while the TST of ectodermal deep tissue aggregates remained low.
source: We tested the first possibility and found that the TST of mesodermal deep tissue aggregates (as in Figure 5D and E, left) remained low until after Stage 10, when it increased more than twofold, while the TST of ectodermal deep tissue aggregates remained low (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 5F.

claim: The simplest explanation consistent with the data is that the self-affinity of the deep IMZ cells, and hence TST, increases, which in the absence of other changes results in an increased IFT and a decreased spreading of the epithelial layer.
source: Thus, the simplest explanation consistent with our data is that the self-affinity of the deep IMZ cells, and hence TST, increases, which in the absence of other changes results in an increased IFT and a decreased spreading of the epithelial layer, whereas the low IFT of the deep ectoderm with respect to the epithelium allows epithelial spreading.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the results presented.

claim: Control wonton explants, filled with ectodermal (animal cap, AC) deep tissue, did not increase their IFT with respect to the epithelium during gastrulation, whereas wontons filled with deep DIMZ increased their IFT from levels similar to those seen in AC controls prior to the onset of gastrulation, to roughly fourfold higher than the AC controls over the first two hours of gastrulation.
source: As in the parallel plate compression tests, control wonton explants, filled with ectodermal (animal cap, AC) deep tissue, did not increase their IFT with respect to the epithelium during gastrulation, whereas wontons filled with deep DIMZ increased their IFT from levels similar to those seen in AC controls prior to the onset of gastrulation, to roughly fourfold higher than the AC controls over the first two hours of gastrulation (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 5H.

claim: TST measured from time lapse movies of deep cell aggregates of dorsal and ventral IMZ using ADSA showed little change in TST until about Stage 10 (G0), at which point both began to increase through Stage 10.5 (G + 2 h), when the DIMZ tissue plateaued.
source: We also measured TST from time lapse movies of deep cell aggregates of dorsal and ventral IMZ (Video 14) using ADSA; these showed little change in TST until about Stage 10 (G0), at which point both began to increase through Stage 10.5 (G + 2 h) (Figure 5I), when the DIMZ tissue plateaued, consistent with the onset of a transition to CE.
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 5I and Video 14.

claim: The TST measurements by parallel plate compression were in agreement with previous TST measurements of these tissues.
source: Whereas our TST measurements by parallel plate compression were in agreement with previous TST measurements of these tissues (David et al., 2009; Luu et al., 2011; David et al., 2014), our ADSA measurements were about 10-fold lower for both TST and IFT (compare Figure 5C and F to H,I).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding and supported by Figure 5C, 5F, 5H, 5I, and citations to David et al., 2009; Luu et al., 2011; David et al., 2014.

claim: ADSA measurements were about 10-fold lower for both TST and IFT compared to parallel plate compression measurements.
source: Whereas our TST measurements by parallel plate compression were in agreement with previous TST measurements of these tissues (David et al., 2009; Luu et al., 2011; David et al., 2014), our ADSA measurements were about 10-fold lower for both TST and IFT (compare Figure 5C and F to H,I).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding and supported by Figure 5C, 5F, 5H, 5I.

claim: Both parallel plate and ADSA measurements showed similar increases in IFT and TST of mesodermal tissues around the onset of gastrulation.
source: Notably, however, both our parallel plate and ADSA measurements showed similar increases in IFT and TST of mesodermal tissues around the onset of gastrulation.
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study.

claim: The increase in IFT between the deep and superficial epithelial tissues in the IMZ was not seen in the IFT between the deep and superficial tissues of the ectoderm (i.e. animal cap).
source: Together, these results indicate an increase in the TST of deep IMZ tissue during CT, consistent with increased cell–cell affinity within the deep mesoderm. Importantly, the increase in IFT between the deep and superficial epithelial tissues in the IMZ was not seen in the IFT between the deep and superficial tissues of the ectoderm (i.e. animal cap).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study.

claim: Affinity between deep ectoderm and epithelium of the NIMZ increases between G-1h and G0.
source: Moreover, the fact that ectodermal epithelium did not spread over deep ectoderm of the NIMZ prior to G-1h, but did by G0 (Figure 4C; Shook, unpublished observations), suggests that affinity between these tissues increases between these times.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the results presented and supported by Figure 4C and unpublished observations.

claim: The increase of IFT between deep and epithelial IMZ would be expected to cause an annular (ring-shaped) IMZ to decrease its surface area, that is to converge and thicken.
source: The increase of IFT between deep and epithelial IMZ would be expected to cause an annular (ring-shaped) IMZ to decrease its surface area, that is to converge and thicken.
evidence: The claim is stated as an inference.

claim: Explant epithelial cell heights were initially not significantly different from those in intact embryos (P = 0.18, for both dorsal and ventral, n = 3 or 4), confirming that the explant procedure did not alter cell height.
source: Explant epithelial cell heights were initially not significantly different from those in intact embryos (P = 0.18, for both dorsal and ventral, n = 3 or 4), confirming that the explant procedure did not alter cell height.
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study with statistical analysis.

claim: Explant epithelial cells subsequently thinned by 5–10%, rather than thickening, while whole embryo epithelial cells thinned by 25–30%, as expected.
source: However, explant epithelial cells subsequently thinned by 5–10%, rather than thickening, while whole embryo epithelial cells thinned by 25–30%, as expected (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The increase in force due to thickening of wontons containing deep IMZ (mesoderm) tested over 30 min, beginning from between G-0.5h to +2.2 h for dorsal IMZ (0.31 μN, SEM = 0.066, n = 7) and from G + 1.3 h to +3.6 h for ventral IMZ (0.27 μN, SEM = 0.023, n = 4), was similar to the previously observed convergence forces from G0 to G + 2 h (about 0.35μN).
source: The increase in force due to thickening of wontons containing deep IMZ (mesoderm) tested over 30 min, beginning from between G-0.5h to +2.2 h for dorsal IMZ (0.31 μN, SEM = 0.066, n = 7) and from G + 1.3 h to +3.6 h for ventral IMZ (0.27 μN, SEM = 0.023, n = 4), was similar to the previously observed convergence forces from G0 to G + 2 h (about 0.35μN) (Shook et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by a citation to Shook et al., 2018.

claim: AC and NIMZ tissue showed little if any increase in thickening force over intervals beginning from G-1h to G + 3.2 h (0.016 μN, SEM = 0.010, n = 7).
source: AC and NIMZ tissue showed little if any increase in thickening force over intervals beginning from G-1h to G + 3.2 h (0.016 μN, SEM = 0.010, n = 7).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study.

claim: Thickening forces were not observed in IMZ explants prior to Stage 10- (G-0.7h; n = 2).
source: Thickening forces were not observed in IMZ explants prior to Stage 10- (G-0.7h; n = 2).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study.

claim: DIMZ wontons showed stress-relaxation as expected of a visco-elastic material, then plateaued for some time before pushing back with increasing force, which on average began at G-41m (G-0.7h, Stage 10-; n = 7, SEM = 1.1 min).
source: In most cases, explants showed stress-relaxation as expected of a visco-elastic material, then plateaued for some time before pushing back with increasing force (Figure 5—figure supplement 2E). On average, this began at G-41m (G-0.7h, Stage 10-; n = 7, SEM = 1.1 min).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 2E.

claim: The average increase in force from the initial, applied force, or from the force at the onset of increased rate of increase at g-0.7h in the exceptional case, was 0.48 μN (n = 5, SEM = 0.11).
source: The average increase in force from the initial, applied force, or from the force at the onset of increased rate of increase at g-0.7h in the exceptional case, was 0.48 μN (n = 5, SEM = 0.11).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study.

claim: AC sandwiches began to decrease the push-back force at G-0.7h (n = 4).
source: AC sandwiches instead began to decrease the push-back force at G-0.7h (n = 4) (data not shown), perhaps associated with the onset of rapid radial intercalation driving epiboly around this time (Keller, 1980), during which deep ectodermal cells actively migrate toward the superficial epithelium (Szabó et al., 2016), causing the deep tissue to spread and thin.
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by citations to Keller, 1980 and Szabó et al., 2016.

claim: With a contour length of Li = 1.2 mm, the expected force of shortening along the long axis of a D180 explant would be F = 0.26 μN, which is indeed close to the convergence force measured in the same explants, of about 0.3 μN from G0 to G + 2 h.
source: With a contour length of Li = 1.2 mm, the expected force of shortening along the long axis of a D180 explant would be F = 0.26 μN, which is indeed close to the convergence force measured in the same explants, of about 0.3 μN from G0 to G + 2 h (Shook et al., 2018) and our observations here that dorsal IMZ wonton explants can generated about 0.3 μN of thickening force over 30 min.
evidence: The claim is stated as a calculation and comparison with measured forces, supported by a citation to Shook et al., 2018.

claim: The IFT could be responsible for generating the measured convergence forces during CT.
source: Thus, the IFT could be responsible for generating the measured convergence forces during CT.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the calculations and measurements presented.

claim: In explants of deep ventral IMZ +NIMZ (VMZ) under cover glass, cells from the deep IMZ engulf the deep NIMZ tissue, migrating around the sides of it, and to a lesser extent, over its face, throughout gastrulation.
source: However, in explants of deep ventral IMZ +NIMZ (VMZ) under cover glass (Materials and methods), cells from the deep IMZ engulf the deep NIMZ tissue, migrating around the sides of it, and to a lesser extent, over its face, throughout gastrulation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F, VMZ; Video 16*, Video 17*).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 2F, Video 16, and Video 17.

claim: Immunohistochemistry showed that C-cadherin and actin expression were similar across all types of cell junctions (deep-deep, superficial-superficial, deep-superficial) at both Stage 9–9.5 and Stage 10.
source: However, immunohistochemistry showed that C-cadherin and actin expression were similar across all types of cell junctions (deep-deep, superficial-superficial, deep-superficial) at both Stage 9–9.5 and Stage 10; pMLC expression was more mosaic, but, on average, also similar across all junctions at both stages (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-D).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-D.

claim: pMLC expression was more mosaic, but, on average, also similar across all junctions at both Stage 9–9.5 and Stage 10.
source: However, immunohistochemistry showed that C-cadherin and actin expression were similar across all types of cell junctions (deep-deep, superficial-superficial, deep-superficial) at both Stage 9–9.5 and Stage 10; pMLC expression was more mosaic, but, on average, also similar across all junctions at both stages (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-D).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-D.

claim: Some other mechanisms, perhaps affecting the activities or turnover of cadherin, actin, or pMLC, regulate affinity between deep and superficial cells, and therefore the change in IFT between them.
source: These results suggest that some other mechanisms, perhaps affecting the activities or turnover of these molecules, regulate affinity between deep and superficial cells, and therefore the change in IFT between them (see Discussion).
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the results presented.

claim: Deep IMZ cells show the same type of low-level 'jostling' behavior both before and after Stage 10-.
source: Deep IMZ cells show the same type of low-level 'jostling' behavior both before and after Stage 10- (e.g. Video 18), with similar levels of compaction at the tissue surface, broken locally as surface cells divided, similar rates of randomly oriented cell division and small amounts of random cell movement, with larger movements due to the cell divisions.
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Video 18.

claim: No significant changes were seen for any metric of cell motility, including movement rate, perimeter change, circularity or length-width ratio, between Stage 9–9.5 and Stage 10.
source: Cell outlines were traced every 2–2.5 minutes and several parameters were extracted for comparison. We saw no significant changes for any metric, including movement rate, perimeter change, circularity or length-width ratio (Figure 5—figure supplement 3F-I).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 3F-I.

claim: No changes were seen in frequency of cell division, net cell movement, orientation of longest axis, or fraction of interstitial spaces between Stage 9–9.5 and Stage 10.
source: We also saw no changes in frequency of cell division, net cell movement, orientation of longest axis, or fraction of interstitial spaces (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study.

claim: Mesodermal cells plated on C-cadherin-Fc spread as early as tested (Stage 9, G-2h), interrupted by partial contractions and detachment from adjacent cells during cell divisions.
source: Whereas mesodermal cells plated on fibronectin will not begin to spread until near Stage 10 (Ramos et al., 1996) (Shook, personal observations), cells spread on C-cadherin-Fc as early as tested (Stage 9, G-2h), interrupted by partial contractions and detachment from adjacent cells during cell divisions (Video 20).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Video 20 and a citation to Ramos et al., 1996.

claim: Spreading of cells on C-cadherin-Fc continued at a fairly constant rate both before and after Stage 10-.
source: Spreading continued at a fairly constant rate both before and after Stage 10- (Figure 5—figure supplement 3J).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 3J.

claim: No differences in the frequency of cell division were observed before or after Stage 10-.
source: No differences in the frequency of cell division were observed before or after Stage 10- (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study.

claim: Changes in cadherin dependent deep cell motility or deep cell contact behavior are not involved in the increase in IFT between deep and superficial cells.
source: These results suggest that changes in cadherin dependent deep cell motility or deep cell contact behavior are not involved in the increase in IFT between deep and superficial cells.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the results presented.

claim: The rate of convergence of the IMZ in unconstrained giant sandwich explants remains constant before and after Stage 10-.
source: Our result that the rate of convergence of the IMZ in unconstrained giant sandwich explants remains constant before and after Stage 10- supports the idea that it is the affinity between superficial and deep, rather than any change in deep cell motility, at least with respect to other deep cells, that is responsible for the increased force production by the IMZ.
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study.

claim: Pre-involution convergence of the IMZ of normal embryos occurs at a similar rate in the dorsal, lateral and ventral regions during early gastrulation.
source: Pre-involution convergence of the IMZ of normal embryos, measured by tracing fiduciary points across the IMZ surface over time (Figure 6—figure supplement 2; Materials and methods), occurs at a similar rate in the dorsal, lateral and ventral regions during early gastrulation (Figure 6A, left column; 6B; Video 1*).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 6A, 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 2, and Video 1.

claim: Convergence begins earlier dorsally, as the apical constriction of the dorsal bottle cells begins at Stage 10- (G-0.7h) and culminates at Stage 10+ (G + 0.5 h).
source: Convergence begins earlier dorsally (Figure 6B, blue line), as the apical constriction of the dorsal bottle cells begins at Stage 10- (G-0.7h) and culminates at Stage 10+ (G + 0.5 h) (see Hardin and Keller, 1988).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 6B and a citation to Hardin and Keller, 1988.

claim: The progression of apical constriction of the bottle cells begins about an hour later around the lateral and then ventral sides of the blastopore.
source: The progression of apical constriction of the bottle cells begins about an hour later around the lateral and then ventral sides of the blastopore (Figure 6A, left column, Stage 10–10.5; Video 1).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 6A and Video 1.

claim: Removal of bottle cells does not change the rate of blastopore closure, which is dependent only on deep IMZ tissue.
source: Although the bottle cells exert tension on the superficial layer above the blastopore, their removal does not change the rate of blastopore closure, which is dependent only on deep IMZ tissue (Keller, 1981; Hardin and Keller, 1988).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Keller, 1981 and Hardin and Keller, 1988.

claim: The pattern of isotropic convergence of the pre-involution IMZ, excepting the first hour, continues throughout gastrulation, at least until Stage 12.5.
source: The pattern of isotropic convergence of the pre-involution IMZ, excepting the first hour, continues throughout gastrulation, at least until Stage 12.5 (Keller and Danilchik, 1988).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Keller and Danilchik, 1988.

claim: There is a highly anisotropic movement directed toward the blastopore from mid-gastrulation onward.
source: There is however a highly anisotropic movement directed toward the blastopore from mid-gastrulation onward (Keller and Danilchik, 1988; Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Keller and Danilchik, 1988 and Video 1.

claim: The highly anisotropic movement toward the blastopore results from mechanical coupling of the pre-involution IMZ to the tissues bordering it, the post-involution mesoderm on the inside and the posterior neural tissues on the outside, both of which are undergoing highly anisotropic CE.
source: This results from mechanical coupling of the pre-involution IMZ to the tissues bordering it, the post-involution mesoderm on the inside and the posterior neural tissues on the outside, both of which are undergoing highly anisotropic CE and thus push the dorsal blastopore lip toward the ventral side of the embryo (see Discussion and Keller and Danilchik, 1988; Figure 6A, left column, compare Stage 10.5–12; Video 1).
evidence: The claim is stated as an explanation and supported by Figure 6A, Video 1, and a citation to Keller and Danilchik, 1988.

claim: In embryos ventralized by UV irradiation of the vegetal hemisphere before first cleavage, Spemann's Organizer is not induced, the dorsal-ventral axis is lost and all tissue types default to ventral.
source: In embryos ventralized by UV irradiation of the vegetal hemisphere before first cleavage, Spemann's Organizer is not induced, the dorsal-ventral axis is lost and all tissue types default to ventral (see Scharf and Gerhart, 1980).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Scharf and Gerhart, 1980.

claim: Ventralized embryos initiate bottle cell formation at nearly the same time all around the embryo at about control Stage 10.5, when normal embryos complete bottle cell formation ventrally.
source: These embryos initiate bottle cell formation at nearly the same time all around the embryo at about control Stage 10.5 (Figure 6A, right column, Stage 10.5, pointers), when normal embryos complete bottle cell formation ventrally (Figure 6A, left column, Stage 10.5).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 6A.

claim: Convergence occurs uniformly around the IMZ in ventralized embryos, driving symmetrical blastopore closure around the VE.
source: Convergence occurs uniformly around the IMZ, driving symmetrical blastopore closure around the VE (Figure 6, right column; Video 1) but begins later and proceeds more slowly than in normal embryos (Figure 6B, black line).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 6 and Video 1.

claim: Convergence in ventralized embryos begins later and proceeds more slowly than in normal embryos.
source: Convergence occurs uniformly around the IMZ, driving symmetrical blastopore closure around the VE (Figure 6, right column; Video 1) but begins later and proceeds more slowly than in normal embryos (Figure 6B, black line).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 6B and Video 1.

claim: Rates of blastopore closure, based on the area of the exposed VE, are similar in normal and ventralized embryos but show a delay of 1–2 hr in the extent of BP closure in ventralized embryos.
source: Rates of blastopore closure, based on the area of the exposed VE, are similar in normal and ventralized embryos but show a delay of 1–2 hr in the extent of BP closure in ventralized embryos (Figure 6C, cf. red and magenta lines), consistent with the delay of bottle cell formation and convergence in ventralized embryos (Figure 6A and B), and suggesting that CE and CT are equally effective at driving blastopore closure.
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 6C, 6A, and 6B.

claim: CE and CT are equally effective at driving blastopore closure.
source: Rates of blastopore closure, based on the area of the exposed VE, are similar in normal and ventralized embryos but show a delay of 1–2 hr in the extent of BP closure in ventralized embryos (Figure 6C, cf. red and magenta lines), consistent with the delay of bottle cell formation and convergence in ventralized embryos (Figure 6A and B), and suggesting that CE and CT are equally effective at driving blastopore closure.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the results presented.

claim: Involution of the IMZ in ventralized embryos begins more slowly compared to normal embryos and is delayed by 3–4 hr.
source: On the other hand, involution of the IMZ in ventralized embryos begins more slowly compared to normal embryos and is delayed by 3–4 hr (Figure 6C, light and dark blue lines).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 6C.

claim: Blastopore closure and convergence of the entire circumference of the IMZ around the blastopore begin well before the onset of CE.
source: These results demonstrate that blastopore closure and convergence of the entire circumference of the IMZ around the blastopore begin well before the onset of CE, that CT accounts for the isotropic convergence of the pre-involution IMZ around the BP, despite the highly anisotropic movements of CE in post-involution mesoderm, and that CT is patterned and can drive BP closure independently of CE.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the results presented.

claim: CT accounts for the isotropic convergence of the pre-involution IMZ around the BP, despite the highly anisotropic movements of CE in post-involution mesoderm.

claim: Cells begin expressing MIB at Stage 10.5 (G + 2 h), as they progressively involute in the intact embryo, and begin to express MIB at the same time in explants.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Shih and Keller, 1992a and Lane and Keller, 1997.

claim: The tissues undergoing CE extend vegetally from the thickened band of tissue comprising the IMZ of sandwich explants.
source: It has been known for some time that the tissues undergoing CE extend vegetally from the thickened band of tissue comprising the IMZ of sandwich explants (see Discussion and Keller and Danilchik, 1988), especially in larger, giant explants (Poznanski et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Keller and Danilchik, 1988 and Poznanski et al., 1997.

claim: The early onset of the thickening and convergence, of the changes in affinity between deep and superficial layers, and in particular, of the initial force production prior to the onset of CE at Stage 10.5 are definitive evidence that IMZ cells first undergo CT and then transition into expressing CE.
source: But the early onset of the thickening and convergence (Figure 2), of the changes in affinity between deep and superficial layers (Figure 4), and in particular, of the initial force production (Shook et al., 2018; Figure 5G, Figure 5—figure supplement 2E) prior to the onset of CE at Stage 10.5 are definitive evidence that IMZ cells first undergo CT and then transition into expressing CE.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the results presented and supported by Figure 2, Figure 4, Figure 5G, Figure 5—figure supplement 2E, and a citation to Shook et al., 2018.

claim: The transition to MIB begins in the presumptive anterior notochordal and somitic tissue, near the dorsal midline and progresses in an arc-shaped front proceeding animally (the toward the presumptive posterior) in the notochordal mesoderm and laterally (also toward the presumptive posterior) in the somitic mesoderm.
source: The transition to MIB begins in the presumptive anterior notochordal and somitic tissue, near the dorsal midline (Figure 1C, St 10.5) and progresses in an arc-shaped front proceeding animally (the toward the presumptive posterior) in the notochordal mesoderm and laterally (also toward the presumptive posterior) in the somitic mesoderm.
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding and supported by Figure 1C.

claim: The transition to MIB continues to pull cells from the lower edge of the thickened region formed by CT, which remains as a relatively thick 'collar' across the upper, animal portion of the IMZ (that part abutting the vegetal edge of the NIMZ at the LI) throughout gastrulation as the pre-involution portion continues to express CT.
source: It continues to pull cells from the lower edge of the thickened region formed by CT (Figure 1C, St 10.5–12+), which remains as a relatively thick 'collar' across the upper, animal portion of the IMZ (that part abutting the vegetal edge of the NIMZ at the LI) throughout gastrulation as the pre-involution portion continues to express CT (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding and supported by Figure 1C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The progressive transition from CT to MIB results in the progressive anterior to posterior convergence and extension of the axial and paraxial tissue in explants, which occurs post-involution in the intact embryo.
source: This progressive transition from CT to MIB results in the progressive anterior to posterior convergence and extension of the axial and paraxial tissue in explants (Shih and Keller, 1992a; Figures 1C and 2A, Video 2*), which occurs post-involution in the intact embryo.
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding and supported by Figure 1C, Figure 2A, Video 2, and a citation to Shih and Keller, 1992a.

claim: In the embryo, CT is generating tension around the outside of the blastopore while MIB is generating tension around the inside; these forces act in parallel to close the blastopore and promote involution.
source: In the embryo, CT is generating tension around the outside of the blastopore while MIB is generating tension around the inside; these forces act in parallel to close the blastopore and promote involution (See Discussion).
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion.

claim: In deep dorsal IMZ +NIMZ (DMZ) explants lacking epithelium and cultured under a cover glass, just like deep VMZ explants, deep DMZ explants initially show engulfment of NIMZ by IMZ, but in DMZ explants the engulfment is reversed at Stage 10.5, whereas in deep VMZ explants it is not.
source: Another behavior associated with the CT to CE transition is seen in deep dorsal IMZ +NIMZ (DMZ) explants lacking epithelium and cultured under a cover glass (see Materials and methods). Just like deep VMZ explants, deep DMZ explants initially show engulfment of NIMZ by IMZ, but in DMZ explants the engulfment is reversed at Stage 10.5, whereas in deep VMZ explants it is not (Figure 5—figure supplement 2F; Video 21*).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 2F and Video 21.

claim: The reversal of engulfment in DMZ explants at Stage 10.5 indicates a change in cell properties in dorsal but not ventral deep tissue, and since it coincides with the onset of MIB, it is likely to be associated with the transition that cell behavior.
source: This indicates a change in cell properties in dorsal but not ventral deep tissue, and since it coincides with the onset of MIB, it is likely to be associated with the transition that cell behavior.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the results presented.

claim: MIB involves bipolar, mediolateral extension of protrusions, their attachment to neighboring cells via C-cadherin adhesion molecules, and polarized pulsatile actomyosin contractility, in a planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway dependent manner.
source: MIB involves bipolar, mediolateral extension of protrusions, their attachment to neighboring cells via C-cadherin adhesion molecules, and polarized pulsatile actomyosin contractility, in a planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway dependent manner (Skoglund et al., 2008; Kim and Davidson, 2011; Pfister et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Skoglund et al., 2008; Kim and Davidson, 2011; Pfister et al., 2016.

claim: MIB exerts a cell-on-cell traction that cumulatively generates the mediolateral tension that intercalates the cells and generates tissue level forces.
source: MIB thereby exerts a cell-on-cell traction that cumulatively generates the mediolateral tension that intercalates the cells and generates tissue level forces (Skoglund et al., 2008; Pfister et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Skoglund et al., 2008 and Pfister et al., 2016.

claim: The forces generated by MIB are dependent on MRLC regulation of myosin heavy chain IIB (MHC IIB) contractility.
source: These forces are dependent on MRLC regulation of myosin heavy chain IIB (MHC IIB) contractility (Skoglund et al., 2008; Kim and Davidson, 2011; Pfister et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Skoglund et al., 2008; Kim and Davidson, 2011; Pfister et al., 2016.

claim: MHC IIB is up-regulated in dorsal tissues expressing CE.
source: MHC IIB is up-regulated in dorsal tissues expressing CE (Kelley et al., 1996; Bhatia-Dey et al., 1998)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kelley et al., 1996 and Bhatia-Dey et al., 1998.

claim: A morpholino (MO) knock down of MHC IIB strongly inhibits blastopore closure in normal embryos that express CE.
source: and a morpholino (MO) knock down of MHC IIB strongly inhibits blastopore closure in normal embryos that express CE (Skoglund et al., 2008; Figure 7A, compare first to second column)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Skoglund et al., 2008 and Figure 7A.

claim: The same dose of MHC IIB MO only mildly retards blastopore closure in ventralized embryos.
source: whereas the same dose of MHC IIB MO only mildly retards blastopore closure in ventralized embryos (Figure 7A, compare third to fourth column)(Video 22*).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study and supported by Figure 7A and Video 22.

claim: MHC IIB MO caused a significant decline in frequency of blastopore closure when injected into normal embryos compared to un-injected controls (p < 0.001, n = 61 vs 82).
source: MHC IIB MO caused a significant decline in frequency of blastopore closure when injected into normal embryos compared to un-injected controls (Figure 7B; p < 0.001, n = 61 vs 82)
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study with statistical analysis and supported by Figure 7B.

claim: Injected normal embryos had a lower frequency of blastopore closure than injected ventralized embryos (p < 0.001, n = 61 vs 31).
source: injected normal embryos also had a lower frequency of blastopore closure than injected ventralized embryos (Figure 7B; p < 0.001, n = 61 vs 31; data from 4 different clutches of eggs).
evidence: The claim is stated as a finding of the study with statistical analysis and supported by Figure 7B.

source: This suggests that CE is strongly dependent on MHC II B, whereas CT is not.
evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion based on the results presented.

evidence: The claim is stated as a conclusion and supported by a citation to Rolo, 2007.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sokol, 1996; Heisenberg et al., 2000; Tada and Smith, 2000; Wallingford et al., 2000.
